title: An error budget for political-bias measurement in large language models: data and code
description:
Raw per-trial data, scoring adapters, and statistical-analysis code for "An error budget for political-bias measurement in large language models." Nineteen large language models were administered up to four standardized political-orientation instruments (Political Compass, 8Values, SapplyValues, Pew Research Center's 2026 Political Typology) repeatedly, alongside factorial designs varying asker identity, instrument contamination, and response format, decomposing a measured political position into variance from model identity, instrument choice, and trial noise.

Includes: raw per-trial administrations (data/), authoritative scoring adapters and collection scripts (scoring/), and the statistical-analysis pipeline that reproduces every number reported in the paper from this data.

Use of AI tools. Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) was used only as a coding tool, interactively between May 2025 and November 2026 through a paid subscription: it helped write and refactor the Python data-collection, scoring, analysis and figure code. It was not used to write or edit the manuscript text, to write the questionnaire item variants, or to find or summarise references; it generated no data and is not an author. The figures were drawn by the released scripts, and no image was generated by AI. Separately, as part of the method, a language model (gpt-4o-mini) rated free-text answers in the response-format design; the headline results use each instrument's own scoring key. The language models studied here are the objects of measurement; they were not used to simulate human respondents, and the paper makes no claim about human samples. The author reviewed all output, checked that every cited source exists and is described accurately, re-derived every reported number from the raw data with the released scripts, and takes full responsibility for the content.
